# Prefetch efficiency versus ARC

**We reduced prefetch waste, but did not establish a repeatable serving frontier better than ARC.** Keep these controls experimental; no canonical defaults were changed.

## Why usefulness was near 3%

Retrospective ledger evaluation of the prior 672 MiB KV run found 42 completed copies: 41 were reclaimed for demand, accounting for 4.184 GB of 4.321 GB speculative traffic. Their median reservation lifetime was only 146 ms. The single useful copy supplied 136.7 MB. This is direct evidence of copy-and-reclaim churn, not evidence that numerical ranking alone caused the slowdown. Attribution to the intended request is conservative; unrelated reuse is not credited. The new default run measured 5.87%, showing scheduling variability rather than a universal 3% constant. See [historical waste ledger](historical-waste.json).

## New experiments

Same RTX 2080 Ti WSL, cached official AWQ Qwen2.5-7B, FP16 KV, frozen shared-prefix/JIT source and strict validator from the prior frontier. CPU cache stays 3.5 GiB. Workload stays 24 public agent sessions, eight active sequences, three actual-output turns, 96-token/EOS output cap and seeded private 0–12 s simulated tool waits. Policy receives only observed prefixes/current state and a fixed public estimate, never future return content/deadlines. Each accepted run completes 72 requests.

Three mechanisms were screened:

- Reduce maximum speculative reservation from 60% to 30% or 15% of the pool. This is a concurrent reservation cap, not a cumulative traffic limit.
- Protect the largest known waiting prompt before speculative allocation. This suppressed all transfers at the small pool and did not recover throughput; rejected as too conservative.
- After an actually completed copy is reclaimed for demand, suppress the same exact source for five seconds. Keep at most 256 source fingerprints. Other sources and ordinary demand restoration are unaffected. This private negative-cache candidate changes admission, not scoring math, ownership or fence handling.

### Small-pool screen: 672 MiB configured KV

|Arm|Output tok/s|p95 first token s|Completed prefetch GB|Useful %|Unused GB|
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|cap 0.6|44.36|51.84|1.594|5.87|1.500|
|cap 0.15|46.84|46.75|1.258|7.44|1.164|
|cap 0.3|41.35|58.62|3.379|3.80|3.251|
|headroom 0.6|44.58|53.02|0.000|—|0.000|
|ARC|47.88|49.11|0.000|—|0.000|
|backoff 0.6|44.63|51.03|0.748|12.52|0.654|

Backoff preserves the same 93.6 MB of named-demand consumption as the fresh default, increases utilization from 5.87% to 12.52%, and reduces unused transfers by 56.4%. Throughput rises only 0.61% and remains 6.80% below ARC. The 15% cap improves over default but remains 2.18% below ARC throughput; its p95 latency is 4.81% lower in this single pair. The 30% cap increases cumulative traffic and is slower. Do not infer a smooth relationship between the cap and lifetime traffic.

### Near-knee screen: 1,792 MiB configured KV

|Arm / partition|Output tok/s|p95 first token s|Completed prefetch GB|Useful %|TPS vs matched ARC %|
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|ARC / 1103|79.98|20.12|0.000|—|+0.00|
|cap 0.15 / 1103|81.08|20.22|0.250|78.31|+1.37|
|backoff 0.6 / 1103|80.32|20.20|1.282|52.68|+0.42|
|cap 0.6 / 1103|80.48|20.24|1.258|51.79|+0.62|
|cap 0.15 / 2207|68.05|23.83|0.269|52.90|-0.48|
|ARC / 2207|68.38|23.71|0.000|—|+0.00|
|ARC / 3301|83.46|17.70|0.000|—|+0.00|
|cap 0.15 / 3301|83.10|17.87|0.541|51.86|-0.43|

At partition 1103, cap15 has 78.3% utilization versus the fresh default’s 51.8%. It cuts completed traffic by 80.2% and unused traffic by 91.1%, but consumption falls from 651 MB to 195 MB and useful adoptions fall from five to two. Its throughput gain over the fresh default is only 0.75%. It is a waste/coverage trade-off, not stronger prediction.

The three cap15/ARC throughput differences are **+1.37%, −0.48%, −0.43%**. Corresponding p95 first-token differences are **+0.47%, +0.54%, +0.97%**. The additional partitions do not repeat the initial speed advantage. Their utilization is 52.9% and 51.9%; the initial 78.3% is not a general result. Partitions vary content and generated histories, so these are descriptive paired observations, not identical-work repetitions or a confidence interval.

## Curves and correctness limits

[Standalone measured frontier PNG](efficiency-frontier.png) · [SVG](efficiency-frontier.svg) · [CSV](RESULTS.csv) · [full rows](RESULTS.json) · [cross-arm inventories](comparisons.json). The first two plot panels use actual peak CUDA allocation including weights/runtime; configured KV is recorded separately. Prior eight-budget points are faded context, not fresh controls or pooled confirmation. New points cover only two valid budgets; no fitted/interpolated frontier or lower-memory capacity win is claimed. A smaller reservation cap does not shrink the startup GPU allocation. None of the new points meets the earlier absolute 15-second p95 first-token criterion.

Fourteen accepted runs provide **1,008 strict request proofs**. All have complete submission/terminal accounting and no surviving owned server descendants. Fourteen focused CPU controls pass for capacity gating/backoff expiry, source isolation, bounded memory and real release-method behavior. These controls do not establish serving KV byte equality or production safety.

**All ten cross-arm comparisons have output differences**, and nine have later prompt/key differences. Those inventories remain explicit, with no numerical-noise waiver. Closed-loop generated histories therefore prevent an exact-work causal speed claim even for the initial favorable point. Per-request strict proofs establish the exercised identity/physical/fence invariants within a run, not cross-arm output equality.

Three additional attempts are excluded: an ARC source-label setup failure before traffic; an ARC client disconnect after 33 response rows/32 strict proofs (not a complete load); and a completed ARC1536 run with 71/72 strict physical proofs. No failed artifact is converted into a passing curve point. The 1,344 MiB control remains a validation hole. Planned candidate1536 measurements were not launched after that failure; matched comparisons moved to 2048. See execution plans/progress and raw directories for exact dispositions.

## Disposition

Retain the 15% cap and bounded reclaim-backoff as opt-in research candidates. The backoff screen directly reduces observed repeated waste; the cap can trade away speculative coverage cheaply. Neither is ready to replace defaults, and neither extends the demonstrated low-VRAM range. There is no repeatable ARC throughput/VRAM or latency/VRAM superiority from these experiments.

A next architectural hypothesis is to reduce long-lived staged reservations by making safely published prefetched pages evictable before request admission. This is unimplemented and unverified; it must preserve shared-prefix identity, publication, native allocator ownership and completion fences. More ranking or a fixed cap alone is not supported as the solution to the low-budget serving gap. The present strict-proof hole also prevents qualifying the intermediate-memory frontier without further investigation.

## Reproduction and custody

[Reproduction](REPRODUCE.md), exact commands/pins in PLAN-v3.json, FOLLOWUP.json, KNEE.json and CONFIRM.json; per-run config/source/runtime/model/corpus pins are inside compressed raw data. [Backoff delta](backoff.patch) and [headroom delta](headroom.patch) are private experiment patches. Canonical pre-existing dirty work is preserved. No commit or push. [Storage and process receipt](STORAGE.json) records removal of task-local plotting dependencies/cache and retention of useful compressed measurements/snapshots. Shared model/serving caches and prior campaigns are protected.
